Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- The test `test_getPackageName_Class()` asserts that the package name of `String[].class` should be `"java.lang"`.
- The bug report states that `ClassUtils.getShortClassName()` adds a semicolon at the end of the class name for array classes.
- Inspecting `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)` calls `getShortClassName(String)` passing `cls.getName()`.
- The implementation of `getShortClassName(String)` does not handle array class names; it just gets the substring after the last dot. Array class names have encoding starting with `[`, for example, `[Ljava.lang.String;`.
- The semicolon is part of the array type descriptor syntax in Java class names, so `getShortClassName` returns `"String;"` instead of `"String"`.
- On the other hand, `getPackageName(Class<?>)` calls `getPackageName(String)` which gets the substring before the last dot.
- `getPackageName(String)` code (lines 244 to 257) does not appear to handle the array encoding either (no code stripped at lines 249-251 which is commented as "Strip array encoding" and "Strip Object type encoding").
- Despite that, the test passes for `getPackageName(String[].class)`, implying `getName()` returns something manageable or the package extraction is unaffected by the trailing semicolon due to the substring operation.
- The root cause of the bug is that `getShortClassName(String)` does not strip or decode the array type syntax (`[L...;`), so the output contains the semicolon at the end for arrays.
- Both package and short class name methods should handle array encoding properly by stripping it before processing the class name.

This analysis explains the incorrect addition of the semicolon in the short class name for arrays and the correct package extraction for the class. The fix is to add array decoding logic in `getShortClassName(String)` and potentially in `getPackageName(String)` as well.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
